_note: This recipe states NO design constants -- no 'd', no 'omega1'. Its "n" block
is now identical to samples_pilot_blind.json's; the two differ only in this
note. Both were arrived at by measurement, saverepo stages 3.0-3.4:
BUDGET 5e10, not 1e8. Stage 3.0 measured what each budget buys for omega1 on
this ladder (planted srw truth, sigma_log = cv/sqrt(n), cv = 0.7741):
budget   per-replicate sd(omega1_hat)   identified at R=3?
1e10     0.39                           marginal
At 1e8 -- this recipe's old budget -- omega1 had a per-replicate spread of ~6
against a truth of 1, so plan.py's unidentified() guard refused every plan the
pilot produced. A real 3-replicate run at 5e10 returns omega1 = 1.0072 +/-
0.0617, a1 = -0.2430 +/- 0.0274, gamma = 0.5002: every constant inside one se.
NO 'd'. Since 2026-08-29 the pilot MEASURES d from the clock and only checks a
declaration against it (src/study/pilot.py:_resolve_d); srw's cost_hint supplies
the allocation's copy, so nothing needs stating here.
NO 'omega1'. It used to say 1.0 -- srw's exact truth. Stage 3.4 showed that
value never reaches the estimator (sweeping it over a range that moves the
allocation by 1e6x moves the fitted omega1 by less than the noise), so keeping
it would not have been a leak. It is dropped because it is the WORST arm: a
5-arm run at this budget, 3 replicates, distinct seeds, gave se(omega1_hat) of
flat (omega1 absent)  0.0076   <-- this recipe
neyman                0.0171
snr, omega1 = 2       0.148
snr, omega1 = 1       0.182    <-- what this recipe used to be, ~24x worse
Decisive: snr with omega1 = 1 is far worse than flat. NOT decisive: the
ordering among the top three, which is ~1.4 sigma on R = 3. Omitting omega1
wins on the point estimate AND needs no design constant, so it is chosen on
both counts; separating flat from neyman properly needs ~8 replicates per arm.
The note this replaces claimed 'a flat n=20000 pilot returned omega1 =
0.06 +/- 0.18; the snr rule at the same wall clock returns 0.98 +/- 0.28'.
Neither reproduces: at that wall clock (~1.01e7) flat gives 3.87 (sd 4.97) and
snr gives 4.92 (sd 6.28) -- neither arm identifies anything at that budget.
